title: Camera-based speed enforcement penalties deferred; tourism funding adjusted
subtitle: Oktoberfest and Scottish Festival top-ups, cultural institution funding review, esports grant, vehicle purchases and mid-year report
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee voted to defer the Administrative Penalty Program bylaws for speed cameras to its October meeting {{vote:m3}}. Staff are to look at warrants for community safety zones, address councillors' concerns, including the doubling of fines, and begin talks with area municipalities. Staff said the program is scheduled to launch in November and that a deferral could affect contracts, hiring and revenue plans.

On tourism, the committee recommended $213,550 in 2024 Cultural Drivers of Tourism funding, with one-time top-ups from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve for KW Oktoberfest and the Cambridge Scottish Festival {{vote:m6}}. It also recommended a $200,000 grant toward a major esports event in June 2025 {{vote:m9}} and supported the Key Cultural Institutions program review {{vote:m8}}.

The committee recommended pre-budget vehicle and ambulance purchases for 2025 and 2026 {{vote:m4}} and received the 2024 mid-year report, which projects an operating surplus. Council still has to adopt these recommendations. Separately, the Chair noted that the acting Chief Financial Officer is leaving the Region.

decisions.detail: The committee deferred the program bylaws and update to its October meeting so staff can examine warrants, address concerns and begin talks with area municipalities.

The committee recommended 2024 allocations of $213,550, plus one-time top-ups from the Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve of $10,600 for KW Oktoberfest and $1,800 for the Cambridge Scottish Festival.
The committee added one-time reserve-funded amounts for KW Oktoberfest and the Cambridge Scottish Festival to the funding recommendation.
The committee recommended supporting the review's recommendations for equitable, stable funding of the Region's Key Cultural Institutions.
The committee recommended a $200,000 Municipal Accommodation Tax Reserve grant to support Explore Waterloo Region's successful bid for a June 2025 esports event.
The committee recommended pre-budget procurement of vehicles, equipment and ambulances scheduled for replacement or expansion in 2025 and 2026.
The committee received the mid-year update and recommended amending the 2024 Capital Budget and 2025-2035 Capital Forecast for various projects.

debate: Oktoberfest delegates said festival costs have risen 30-40% since the pandemic while grants and sponsorships have not kept pace. They said the funding formula does not capture a four-week festival's tourism impact and penalizes lean budgets, and they asked for the reduction to be paused.

On speed cameras, supporters of deferral said fine doubling and the community safety zone criteria were new information to them and that area municipalities had concerns. Opponents said Council had already directed the work, and that staff had hired people and bought equipment for a November launch.

Staff said the Provincial Offences court cannot handle the expected ticket volume. They said fines under the administrative penalty program are roughly double current ones and align with the provincial community safety zone schedule. Surplus revenue would go to a road safety reserve, and appeals on financial hardship are available.

On tourism funding, one councillor questioned relying on applicant-supplied tourist numbers. Another asked how legacy-funded festivals would ever reach the formula if amounts were restored. Staff said the adjustment was one-time and the reserve had enough to cover it.

A councillor sought regional funding balance for Cambridge's Scottish Festival. Another asked whether Drayton's host municipality also funds Drayton Entertainment; staff did not know and offered to find out.
